items.title: Answering 3 remaining questions about NFL shift to open distribution
items.summary: SBJ reports that Ticketmaster's new deal as the NFL's secondary ticketing partner is a seven-year agreement with a fourth-year opt-out tied to how the new open-distribution setup and its technology perform. Under that setup, licensed ticketing companies will be able to sell not only club single-game tickets but also season-ticket holders' resale inventory league-wide, and season tickets make up nearly 90% of team inventory on average. Team sources see it as a win because it widens reach and gives clubs clearer data on how many tickets are resold, by which fans and where, since a ticket resold on a site such as StubHub currently shows up only as a forwarded ticket.
items.what_it_means: Opening up resale across licensed partners gives NFL clubs far better visibility of who actually ends up holding their tickets, which has been a blind spot until now.

items.title: WTA Finals control, media rights fuel WTA's growth strategy
items.summary: Citing The Athletic, SBJ reports that WTA chair Valerie Camillo believes the tour can close its gap with the ATP, which has about twice its revenue and five times its assets, by controlling its high-profile events and media rights. Camillo called off a proposed commercial merger with the ATP, and the WTA has now taken operational control of the WTA Finals and greater control of selling its media rights. Total revenue was $143M in 2024, up from $110M in 2019, and sources say sponsorship has doubled over the past two years to nearly $80M, with revenue expected to pass $300M by 2029.
items.what_it_means: The WTA is betting that owning its biggest event and selling its own rights will grow revenue faster than partnering with the men's tour.

items.title: CFP, ESPN reach deal on 24-team field
items.summary: The College Football Playoff management committee unanimously approved expanding to 24 teams from the 2027-28 season, with ESPN as exclusive worldwide rights holder for the expanded event. SBJ's Austin Karp reports the new deal is worth $1.7B over five years, about $340M a year, on top of ESPN's existing $7.8B CFP agreement through 2031-32. ESPN.com notes the change eliminates the Power 4 conference championship games, starts the season on a Week Zero before Labor Day and ends the regular season on Thanksgiving weekend.
items.what_it_means: ESPN is paying a premium for more playoff inventory, and the conferences are giving up their own championship games to create it.

items.title: Trail Blazers' hot start fuels surge in ticket sales
items.summary: Citing the Portland Business Journal, SBJ reports the Trail Blazers rank second in the NBA for single-game ticket sales, up 76% on last year, with group sales up 32%, as they sit 6-1 atop the Western Conference. That comes despite a summer of tension with the city over funding for Moda Center renovations. The team added 50 courtside seats that season ticket holders quickly bought, and launched a $29 Sixth Man Special that includes a ticket and a $20 food and beverage voucher for select games, which its ticketing chief said owner Tom Dundon was keen on.
items.what_it_means: A winning start is lifting casual and group demand, and the club is pairing premium inventory with low-cost entry offers to capture both ends of it.

items.title: 'Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival' Headlined By Travis Scott, Cardi B, & Justice
items.summary: Rockstar Games has announced Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival, a one-off launch event on 21 November at Mana Wynwood in Miami, two days after the game's 19 November release. Presented with PlayStation and produced by the creators of III Points, it will feature two stages of artists from the game and its soundtrack, including Travis Scott, Cardi B, Don Toliver, Metro Boomin and a Justice DJ set. Tickets are sold through a DICE presale lottery, limited to two per code.
items.what_it_means: A video game launch is being staged as a music festival, using live performance from its own soundtrack to turn a release into an in-person event.

items.title: Fanatics, American Express collaborate on new credit card
items.summary: Fanatics and American Express have launched the Fanatics American Express Card, designed after Topps trading cards, with fans able to pick a favourite player from more than 500 NBA, NFL, UFC and WWE athletes for the card design. The card earns FanCash, Fanatics' loyalty currency, on fandom purchases and everyday spending, redeemable for apparel, trading cards, collectibles, tickets and events such as Fanatics Fest. Cardmembers also get early access to select Topps drops and can enter a Championship Challenge to have their bill paid by predicting all four major US league champions.
items.what_it_means: Fanatics is extending its loyalty currency into everyday spending, so fans earn toward sports merchandise and experiences whenever they use the card.

items.title: WTGL Has 'Surreal' Debut as Newest Women's Sports League
items.summary: WTGL, the indoor team women's golf league modelled on the men's TGL, debuted on Sunday in front of a sell-out crowd at the 1,500-seat SoFi Center in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, with Los Angeles Golf Club beating New York Golf Club 3-1. The league has five teams of five LPGA players, an $11 million season purse and media rights deals with ESPN and Ion, with most matches in primetime on Mondays or Tuesdays. ESPN joined the broadcast 15 minutes late because a college basketball game ran long, a problem TGL has also had, and world number one Nelly Korda has not joined the league.
items.what_it_means: Women's golf is testing whether a short, made-for-TV format can win new audiences, but it still has to compete for its broadcast window.

items.title: Bengals' Madrid trip marked by strong fan turnout, success on and off field
items.summary: Citing the Cincinnati Enquirer and The Athletic, SBJ reports that the Bengals left Madrid with wins on and off the field after a five-day trip. Bengals fans outnumbered Falcons fans at the Bernabeu by a wide margin, even though it was officially an Atlanta home game. Head coach Zac Taylor and quarterback Joe Burrow both praised the turnout, and the club's operations, equipment and marketing teams were credited for planning the trip months in advance.
items.what_it_means: International games are showing that a club's fan base can travel and gather abroad, even when the club is not the designated home team.

items.title: Harlem Globetrotters balance tradition and reinvention in 100th season
items.summary: Citing The New York Times, SBJ reports the Harlem Globetrotters are closing their centennial season while trying to reach new fans without losing the traditions that made them popular. President Keith Dawkins, a former Nickelodeon executive who took over in 2022, has expanded the team's digital presence, documentaries and merchandise. Recent moves include a partnership with Drake's OVO brand, new uniforms by designer Jeff Hamilton, three seasons of a reality series on NBC and Peacock, and active Instagram and TikTok accounts.
items.what_it_means: A century-old entertainment brand is relying on fashion, content and social platforms to stay relevant when its tricks are freely available on YouTube.

items.title: Charlotte Jones reflects on growing role of women in NFL ownership
items.summary: Citing the Dallas Morning News, SBJ reports Cowboys co-owner and chief branding officer Charlotte Jones saying the NFL ownership room has changed dramatically, with a next generation bringing gender diversity that was not there before. She compared the Cowboys' family ownership with the Bengals, where Mike Brown's daughter Katie negotiates contracts and oversees business operations. Data gathered by the Cowboys shows 49.8% of the team's fans are women.
items.what_it_means: Clubs with near-even gender splits in their fan base are seeing that reflected in who runs them, and that has implications for how they market.
